title: Clinical and Immunological Characterization of Anti-GFAP Astrocytopathy Based on Published Cases and Multicentre Patient Cohorts
summary:
In anti-GFAP astrocytopathy, the immune system produces antibodies directed against a protein found in specific supporting cells of the brain and spinal cord (astrocytes), thereby triggering inflammation of the nervous system. The disease is rare and its clinical course, optimal treatment strategies and long-term outcomes remain insufficiently understood. Furthermore, anti-GFAP antibodies are occasionally detected in individuals with other neurological disorders, in whom their presence may not necessarily indicate a clinically relevant disease process.
This study aims to investigate whether the disease typically follows a monophasic or relapsing course, which cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings help distinguish genuine disease from incidental antibody positivity, which treatment strategies have been employed, and what the subsequent clinical outcomes have been.
To this end, existing clinical data from adult patients with confirmed anti-GFAP antibody positivity will be retrospectively analysed across several university hospitals in Germany and Austria. All data will be anonymised prior to analysis. No additional examinations will be performed, and there will be no direct contact with the patients.

interventions.name: Multicentre retrospective analysis of all adult patients (≥ 18 years) with confirmed anti-GFAP antibodies in serum and/or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), detected by cell-based assay, who were diagnosed and/or treated at the participating centres. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Anti-GFAP antibodies detected in serum and/or cerebrospinal fluid using a standardized cell-based assay (CBA)
- Diagnosed and/or treated at one of the participating centers
- Sufficient clinical documentation (clinical presentation, CSF findings and/or disease course)
Exclusion criteria:
- Missing or non-validatable antibody status (no information on the detection method, non-standardized assay, unclear date of testing)
- Insufficient clinical documentation without usable information on clinical presentation, CSF findings or disease course
- Age < 18 years
